To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the oxidation of 1-2-bis(mesoporphyrinyl)-substituted ethanes to the corresponding 1-2-diporphyrinylethylenes is a facile process in organic acids; (2) the mechanism of the oxidation is two-electron oxidation of the dimer followed by protonation of the porphyrin macrocycles; (3) the reaction is catalyzed by Fe(III) ions; and (4) the

(1) the reaction proceeds in several organic acids (H2SO4, CF3CO2H, HCO2H, and H2O), and (2) the mechanism of the oxidation involves the formation of the radical cation of the dimer followed by the protonation of the two meso positions of the two porphin rings.

(i) a facile aerobic oxidation of a porphyrin dimer to a trans-ethylene-bridged species has been observed for the first time; and (ii) the mechanism of the oxidation involves monoprotonation followed by a two electron oxidation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of the oxidation reaction of ethane-bridged porphyrin dimers to trans-ethylene-bridged species.
the mechanism and the kinetics of the aerobic oxidation of the 1,2-ethane bridged porphyrin dimers in the presence of organic acids.
the oxidation of ethane-bridged porphyrin dimers in several organic acids to trans-ethylene-bridged dimers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the oxidation of the ethane-bridged dimers in several organic acids is a two step process.
the oxidation of the dimer to the trans-ethene-bridged species proceeds via the monoprotonation followed by the two electron oxidation.
the reaction is a one-pot, three-step process: (1) monoproticn of the dimer, (2) two-electron oxidation, and (3) elimination of ethane.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the oxidation is a proton-coupled electron transfer process.
the ethane-bridged porphyrin dimers are readily oxidized to the trans-ethene-bridged species by air or other oxidizing agents.
the porphyrin dimer can act as an efficient electron reservoir and the electron transfer from the dimer to oxygen can be accelerated by the presence of a suitable proton acceptor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the oxidation reaction of porphyrin dimers to trans-ethene-bridged species can be carried out in the presence of air in a wide range of acids.
the oxidation reaction is not a free radical chain reaction as previously suggested, but a two-electron oxidation of the dimer to the trans-ethyne dimer.
the oxidation of ethane-bridged porphyrin dimers is an efficient method to prepare trans-ethylene-bridged porphyin dimer.
